title: Observable Stream
description: Build an Observable stream library with creation, transformation operators, and subscription management.

steps.title: Create Observable class
steps.description: Implement an Observable class with a `subscribe()` method that accepts an observer object (next, error, complete handlers). The constructor receives a producer function that wires up the observer. Print the subscription object to console.
hints: The constructor takes a function (observer) => {} that calls observer.next()
subscribe() should return a subscription object with an unsubscribe method
Start with synchronous emission before worrying about async

verification.successMessage: Observable class emits values and returns a valid subscription
verification.failureMessage: Observable did not emit values or subscription object is missing

steps.title: Add creation functions (of, from, interval)
steps.description: Implement static creation functions: `of(...args)` emits each argument in sequence, `from(iterable)` converts arrays and promises to observables, `interval(ms)` emits incrementing numbers at a time interval. Print each emitted value.
hints: of() calls observer.next() for each argument then observer.complete()
from() checks if the input is an array (iterate) or promise (then)
interval() uses setInterval and returns a teardown function to clear it

verification.failureMessage: Creation functions did not emit expected values

steps.title: Implement map and filter operators
steps.description: Build a `.pipe()` method and implement `map(fn)` and `filter(predicate)` as transform operators that return new observables. The pipe method chains operators left-to-right. Print the transformed values.
hints: pipe() reduces over operators: operators.reduce((source, op) => op(source), this)
Each operator returns a function that takes a source observable and returns a new observable
filter re-emits values that pass the predicate, map transforms each value

verification.successMessage: map and filter operators transform values correctly
verification.failureMessage: Transformed values did not match expected results

steps.title: Add merge and concat operators
steps.description: Implement `merge(obs1, obs2)` which subscribes to all observables simultaneously and interleaves their emissions, and `concat(obs1, obs2)` which subscribes to the next only after the previous completes. Print all emitted values.
hints: merge subscribes to all observables at once and forwards all next calls
concat subscribes to the first, buffers the second, subscribes after complete
Both return a new Observable that manages multiple inner subscriptions

verification.successMessage: Merge interleaves and concat sequences emissions correctly
verification.failureMessage: Merge or concat did not produce expected ordering

steps.title: Implement debounce and throttle
steps.description: Implement `debounce(ms)` which emits a value only after a specified silence period, and `throttle(ms)` which emits at most once per time window. Use timers to control emission rates. Print the debounced values.
hints: debounce resets a timer on each emission and only fires when the timer elapses
throttle uses a timestamp to track the last emission and drops intermediate values
Both need cleanup in the teardown function to clear pending timers

verification.successMessage: Debounce and throttle correctly rate-limit emissions
verification.failureMessage: Debounced or throttled values did not appear as expected

steps.title: Add error handling (catchError, retry)
steps.description: Implement `catchError(handler)` which intercepts errors and switches to a fallback observable, and `retry(n)` which resubscribes to the source up to N times on error. Print the recovery path.
hints: catchError catches observer.error() and subscribes to a fallback instead
retry stores the source producer function and re-invokes it on error
After retries exhausted, the error should propagate to the observer

verification.successMessage: Error handling operators catch and recover from errors correctly
verification.failureMessage: Error recovery did not produce expected fallback values

steps.title: Build subscriber with teardown
steps.description: Implement a Subscription class that tracks multiple child subscriptions and supports `unsubscribe()` and `add()`. When unsubscribed, all teardown functions execute and a `closed` flag is set. Print the full lifecycle (subscribe, next, unsubscribe, cleanup).
hints: Subscription stores an array of teardown functions and a closed boolean
unsubscribe() iterates teardown functions in LIFO order and sets closed = true
Observable.subscribe() should return the Subscription so users can manage the lifecycle

verification.successMessage: Subscription lifecycle is tracked correctly from subscribe to teardown
verification.failureMessage: Subscription lifecycle events were not printed in the correct order
